text: To date, only two published studies have endeavored to compare longitudinal hypertrophic adaptations in a variation of superset training versus a traditional training scheme (24). A cohort of 39 resistance-trained men and women were randomly assigned to perform a total-body resistance training program under one of three conditions: (1) perform exercises as pre-exhaustion compound supersets (e.g., pec fly before chest press, leg extension before leg press, and pullover before lat pulldown), (2) perform the same exercises in the same order, but take a 60-second rest interval between sets, or (3) perform the multi-joint exercise before the single-joint movement for each body part with a 60-second rest interval between sets.
